terms.gloss: a policy, a line of conduct
evidence: Sall. Cat. 56.5: aliēnum suīs ratiōnibus, against his policy (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: course, conduct, procedure, plan; in the plural, one’s interests and policy.

terms.gloss: a plan, a measure decided on
evidence: Caes. BG 1.21: quid suī cōnsiliī sit, ostendit (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a practice, a rule one keeps
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.18: oblītum cōnsuētūdinis et īnstitūtī meī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For “it’s my policy”: what one habitually does.

phrases.latin: haec ego ad tē ob eam causam maximē scrībō, ut jam dē tuā quoque ratiōne meditēre
phrases.english: my main reason for writing this is that you should now think about your own policy too

phrases.latin: Dē suā ratiōne interrogātus, ambiguus fit.
phrases.english: When asked about his own policy, he becomes evasive.

sources: Lewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: institutum
